CLAIM UNDER TEST: the 6-node graph H (rows = out-neighbourhoods: 0->{1,2}; 1->{3,5}; 2->{3,4,5}; 3->{0,4,5}; 4->{0,1,3,5}; 5->{0,1,2,3,4}; 19 edges; bidirected pairs {1,5},{2,5},{3,4},{3,5},{4,5}; the unique non-adjacent pair is {1,2}, so the full vertex set is NOT a clique) supports a stable full-support fixed point under the CLAUDE.md s2 convention at P1 (eps=1/101, delta=27/2626, q=1350/1313) and P2 (eps=1/1001, delta=27/26026, q=13500/13013), both legal (eps < delta/(1+delta) = 27/2653 resp. 27/26053) and far below the proven-safe threshold (~805/202), hence a counterexample to the target-free clique conjecture (condition 2 vacuous for full support).

RESULT OF SYNTHESIS: VERIFIED. Five independent exact re-derivations (sympy Rational Routh/Hurwitz + certified root isolation + resultant Sturm count; exact Lyapunov equation with Sylvester criterion + Hurwitz cross-check; Fraction-only Faddeev-LeVerrier/Bareiss with entrywise comparison to ctln.analyze_support; a convention skeptic who fetched Geneson's PDF, tested all four readings A/A^T/comp(A)/comp(A)^T and reproduced Geneson's Theorem 3.2 end-to-end; an eigenvalue skeptic with two certified bounds on max Re(lambda) and full nondegeneracy over all 63 supports) all agree bit-for-bit on det(I-W), x, the 7 characteristic-polynomial coefficients and the 6 Hurwitz minors at both points, with no zero minor (verdict STABLE, not UNDECIDED), x strictly positive with zero residual, and max Re(lambda) certified <= -498/872525 (P1) and <= -23/390905 (P2). Both skeptics ended with verified=true and found no real error. As synthesizer I additionally reconstructed A from the agreed edge list and recomputed everything in fractions.Fraction (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-CLTN/083b78b8-b6de-5340-9343-2e5fdd9085d8/scratchpad/wf_verify2/synth/consistency.py, log consistency.log): every reported exact number reproduces, the 'context' report's symbolic charpoly coefficients in (eps,delta) evaluate exactly to the pointwise numbers at P1 and P2, Orlando D6 = a6*D5 holds, p(-eps)=0, a6 = det(I-W), and the transposed convention gives negative x at nodes 1,3,4 (so no transposition could have manufactured this result). No file under /home/user/CLTN was modified by any verifier (git status clean).

SIGNIFICANCE CAVEAT (not a validity issue): H is non-isomorphic to Geneson's G and to G^T (brute force over 720 permutations; out-degree sequences [2,2,3,3,4,5] vs [2,2,3,4,4,4]), but H = G' - (3->1) + (5->1) for a relabeling G' of G, i.e. one out-edge moved between the in-twin pair {3,5}. This rank-one update provably preserves chi_A, chi_{A+J}, the CTLN full-support characteristic polynomial AND the full-support fixed point identically in (eps,delta,theta). So H is a genuinely new second 6-vertex graph (not in Geneson's paper nor in ipitchford/ctln-six-is-minimal), but it carries no new full-support parameter-region information relative to G: it is a counterexample exactly where G is. The 'new' content is the twin-move equivalence itself and that this graph has no target-free cliques at all (ctln.scan_supports: full support is the only stable FP at P1, P2).

concerns: CLAUDE.md s2 closed form is the transpose of its own entrywise definition: with row-sends A (A[i][j]=1 iff i->j) and W[i][j] = -1+eps iff A[j][i]=1, one gets I - W = -delta I + (1+delta) J - (eps+delta) A^T, not A (checked symbolically for both graphs). Characteristic polynomials are unaffected (transpose-invariant), but fixed points are: taking the closed form literally with row-sends A gives, for G at eps=1/1000, delta=29/25000, x = (-64180625000, -64180625000, 193958275000, 112722025000, -6786725000, 37609375000)/209111857249, i.e. G would not even be a fixed point, whereas the entrywise form reproduces Geneson's certificate vector exactly. Since Stage 0 is marked reproduced, the code presumably uses the entrywise form or stores A transposed; the document should be corrected. I did not read ctln.py (not authorized by the task) so I cannot say which the code does.

The equivalence proved here covers the FULL support only (conditions 1 and 3; condition 2 is vacuous). Proper sub-supports of H and G are not equivalent in general (different principal submatrices), so H's size-5 supports and its nondegeneracy are separate questions; nondegeneracy was verified only at three rational points (eps,delta) = (1/12,11/120), (1/100,29/2500), (1/1000,29/25000).

I did not re-derive G's (hence H's) full parameter region; stability/positivity of H's full support is established here only at the three sampled points plus the symbolic identity with G. Geneson's theorem gives small eps; the ipitchford region claim was not re-verified.

The task text's hint 'bidirected pairs {0,3}?' is wrong: in H the pair {0,3} has only the edge 3->0. The bidirected pairs of H are {1,5},{2,5},{3,4},{3,5},{4,5}; {1,2} is the unique non-adjacent pair (confirmed).

'Cospectral in the compressed sense' understates the situation: H and G are fully cospectral (chi_A, chi_{A+J}, all tr A^k agree) and even share the exact CTLN full-support fixed point; they are distinguished by chi(A^T A) (103 vs 106 lam^4 coefficient) and by the out-degree sequence.

Uniqueness: I showed only that among the 4 labelled graphs with G's twin-class data there are exactly 2 isomorphism classes (G and H). I did not search all 1,540,944 n=6 digraphs for other graphs with the same compressed spectrum, so I cannot say H is the only cospectral mate of G.

The general remark that moving any SET of out-edges between in-twins preserves chi_A, chi_{A+J}, the CTLN full-support char poly and fixed point follows from the same rank-one argument but was machine-verified only for the single-edge case.

Part (d) coverage limits: the arXiv abstract fetch did not include the graph and the PDF fetch summarizer failed on the binary, but the saved PDF was read page-by-page (all 8 pages). The repo was cloned with git (allowed by CLAUDE.md s10b) and scanned mechanically for matrices; graphs described only in prose (the family table) were checked by hand for r=0 only. Only one web search was run; no exhaustive priority search. The repo's small_order_obstructions.json (supports of size <= 5) contains no 6x6 matrices by construction.

The repo's own classification paper (paper/main.tex) states it 'does not claim a topology classification of all CTLNs' and is self-described as not peer-reviewed; its twin lemma was read but not independently re-proved here beyond the 2-vertex class relevant to G/H.
